issues.description: Method name/signature inconsistency for Developer.attend(course:): the problem statement (and the template) require an instance method named attend(course:) on class Developer, taking a parameter course of type Course?; the solution implements the same behavior under a differently named method participateIn(course:) (parameter type Course?). This mismatch between expected API name (attend) and the solution's identifier (participateIn) will confuse students and maintainers and can lead to mismatches when comparing student code to the reference or when tests/tools expect attend(course:).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name/signature consistent across all artifacts. Prefer renaming the solution's participateIn(course:) method to attend(course:) (keeping its implementation and parameter type Course?) so it matches the problem statement and the template. Alternatively, if participateIn is preferred, update the problem statement and template to require participateIn(course:) and adjust tests accordingly.

issues.description: The exercise requires a Developer instance method named attend(course:). The problem statement calls the method attend(course:). The template stub declares func attend(course: Course?) in Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift. However, the solution implementation declares func participateIn(course: Course?) in Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift while the solution's client still calls myself.attend(course:). This name mismatch (attend vs. participateIn) prevents a straightforward mapping from the requirement to the implemented API, will cause compilation errors in the solution, and confuses students about which method they are expected to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution method participateIn(course:) to attend(course:) in Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift (keeping the same parameter type Course?) so the Developer class implements attend(course:) as specified by the problem statement and as called by the client. Alternatively, change all references (problem statement, template, and client) to participateIn, but prefer aligning the solution implementation to the declared attend(course:) to avoid breaking the provided client and student expectations.
